name: Prudent Corporate Advisory Services Ltd
title: Prudent Corporate Advisory Services Ltd - 543527 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 equity AUM rose 1.7% QoQ to INR1.37 lakh crore despite INR1,867 crore MTM drag, with record INR4,137 crore net sales.
summary.overview: Quarterly average AUM reached INR1.43 lakh crore, up 8% QoQ and 21% YoY, while revenue from operations rose 11.8% QoQ and operating profit rose 15.4% QoQ with margin expanding 80 bps to 26.4%. Reported PAT fell 4.1% QoQ to INR71.7 crore because other income dropped about 82% to INR3.8 crore on bond-yield and hybrid-portfolio mark-to-market reversals. Management said the sharp market correction in late October leaves current AUM slightly below the first-half average of INR1.38 lakh crore. The bulk of the call went to a proposed insurance distribution regulation (IDA vs IDE commission gap), where management said insurance is about 12% of PBT and the impact is uncertain.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM up 8% QoQ; MF yield stable at 88-89 bps. Equity AUM share ex-ETF rose from 2.59% to 2.7% YoY; SIP market share rose from 3.49% to 3.73%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution
segments.commentary: Insurance revenue up 35% QoQ; general insurance fresh premium up 54% QoQ and 62% YoY; life fresh premium up 37% QoQ and 45% YoY. Management puts the insurance contribution at about 12% of profit (PBT).

segments.name: Other financial and non-financial products (incl. PMS)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% QoQ, led by PMS distribution; average PMS AUM grew 37% YoY to about INR2,020 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects MF PMS framework to be operational from April 2027; company is applying for MF PMS license via subsidiary renamed Prudent Asset Management Private Limited (formerly Prutech).

Management said that if the insurance proposal were implemented as drafted (IDE renewal commission 5% vs 10% for IDA), it would hurt the insurance business, but called that scenario unlikely; the final regulation is awaited before giving numbers.
Management expects renewal commission cuts to be passed on to POSPs from April onwards, reducing absolute margin on that book.
Company is awaiting SEBI's final FICP framework before launching online bond distribution through its OBPP license.
capex_capacity: Pan-India branch network and tech platform; around 700 sales employees cited as capacity to support distributors moving into MF.
SIF certification: 1,792 distributors certified; SIF AUM nearly INR900 crore.
Onboarded about 3,541 new distributors in H1 FY27, nearly 30% higher than H1 FY26.
demand_pricing: Industry net sales were weak; Prudent's net sales were the highest ever. Management says redemptions are lower than before and SIP cancellations rose.
SIP contributes about 50% of Prudent's gross sales; management said its market-share gains partly reflect this SIP mix in a weak fresh-flow market.

Management said competition from platforms, banks and national distributors is rising, but it is holding market share; it said some large players are moderating payouts after 2-3 years of higher payouts.
Management said MF PMS fee cap of 1% is close to current ~80-90 bps realisation on MF, so margin should be similar.
Commissions as a share of non-insurance operating revenue rose to 62.6% from 61.4% in Q1, which management attributed mainly to a INR2.5 crore additional trail provision (INR1.75 crore booked in Q2).

qa_highlights.question: How would a level playing field between IDEs and IDAs change the economics, and where are insurance margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insurance margins are broadly in line with mutual funds; it will size the opportunity once the final regulation is out, but IDEs need at least parity with IDAs to remain viable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12% insurance profit contribution at risk, and will POSPs survive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entire 12% will not disappear overnight; renewal books may persist, and the impact will be gradual. It gave no firm guidance on the eventual impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will competition for distributors pressure MF payouts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants with higher payouts cannot sustain them long-term and that payouts are moderating; it does not see a margin challenge from new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MF yield rise slightly this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin is static at about 88.8 bps; the uptick reflected one additional revenue day, not mix.

qa_highlights.question: What share of POSPs overlap with MFDs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 90% overlap at family level between MF distributors and POSPs.

qa_highlights.question: Will PMS MF cannibalise MFD business and what realisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PMS MF should attract new distributors, with fee capped at 1%, close to current 80-90 bps earnings, so margin should be similar to MF.

qa_highlights.question: Why did market share gains occur and how much is in small and mid cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed gains to higher net sales, lower redemptions and a SIP-heavy book, noting SIPs are concentrated in small and mid cap; it warned share gains may stall if fresh gross flows recover.

risks_watch: Proposed insurance distribution regulation (IDA 10% vs IDE 5% renewal commission in health): insurance is about 12% of PBT; final rules pending.
Other income is volatile (INR3.8 crore in Q2 vs INR20.8 crore in Q1) due to bond yields and hybrid MTM.
Market correction in late October 2026 means current AUM is slightly below the H1 average; watch SIP cancellations and fresh flows.
Commissions as a share of non-insurance operating revenue rose to 62.6% from 61.4% QoQ; watch payout trends.
Timing and licensing for MF PMS (April 2027) and FICP framework for online bonds.
Market share gains are partly tied to SIP mix and may not persist if fresh gross flows recover.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating performance and market share, but guarded on the insurance regulation, where management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance. Several answers relied on historical analogies and qualitative reassurance. Some answers were disrupted by line drops, leaving parts of the Q&A incomplete.
key_quotes: This is the highest quarterly net sales in our history.
So IDE earn almost 50% less than the agent for exactly the same business.
I don't think entire 12% will disappear overnight.
So practically, you can say that more than 90% overlap is there between mutual fund and the POSP.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly net sales in company history
Helped by one additional revenue day; MF yield 88-89 bps
+37.6% YoY; operating margin 26.1% vs 22.7% last year

growth.why: Q2 FY27 revenue +11.8% QoQ and operating profit +15.4% QoQ with record INR4,137 crore net sales and SIP market share up to 3.73%, but no explicit forward revenue guidance; growth backed by demand/share gains and PMS/MF market entry (April 2027 framework), with insurance commission regulation a key uncertainty.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating margin rose 80 bps QoQ to 26.4% and H1 margin is 26.1% vs 22.7% last year, but renewal commission pass-through to POSPs from April and rising commissions (62.6% of non-insurance revenue vs 61.4% in Q1) cap upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pan-India branch network and about 700 sales staff support distributor onboarding (3,541 new distributors in H1, up ~30% YoY), and the MF PMS framework starts April 2027, but no new physical capacity or dated build-out was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record INR4,137 crore quarterly net sales, SIP market share up to 3.73% from 3.49%, and SIP book up 17.2% YoY to INR1,272 crore, though AUM is slightly below H1 average after the late-October correction and share gains may stall if gross flows recover.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No forward revenue or margin guidance was given, and management stated the 88.8 bps MF yield is sustainable rather than rising.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: A proposed insurance commission cut (IDE renewal at 5% vs 10% for IDA) affects about 12% of PBT; management called the drafted scenario unlikely but gave no quantified impact while the final rule is awaited.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: MF PMS framework is due from April 2027 with a company licence application under way via Prudent Asset Management, and online bond distribution awaits SEBI's FICP framework, with no date given.

rows.label: Insurance distribution regulation (IDA vs IDE commission gap)
rows.why: Insurance is about 12% of PBT and the drafted IDE renewal commission of 5% vs 10% for IDA would hurt the business, but management called that scenario unlikely and the final rule is awaited.

rows.label: MF PMS launch via Prudent Asset Management
rows.why: Management expects the MF PMS framework from April 2027 and the company is applying for the licence; the 1% fee cap is close to the current 80-90 bps MF realisation, so margin should be similar.

rows.label: Other income volatility
rows.why: Other income fell to INR3.8 crore from INR20.8 crore in Q1 on bond-yield and hybrid MTM, so reported PAT can swing even as operating profit grows.

tone.note: Management was confident on record net sales, share gains and operating margin, but guarded on the insurance regulation and gave no quantified impact; analysts pressed on insurance economics and POSP survival, and some Q&A answers were cut off by line drops.
